what: A screen on the wall that shows what a sound is made of: a row of glowing bars, bass notes at the left and bright, high sounds at the right.
how: The sound is chopped into its frequencies (a spectrum) many times a second and each bar is how loud one band of frequencies is. A bass drum lights the left bars; a hi-hat lights the right. The sound passes straight on to OUT unchanged, so you can put it anywhere on a cable. It shows its picture even when nothing downstream is heard.

outs.out: The same sound, passed on untouched.

knobs.range: How many dB (decibels, a measure of loudness) below full level still show as a bar. A bigger range shows quiet detail; a smaller one shows only the loud parts.
knobs.fall: How slowly the bars drop after a loud moment. High and the bars hang and sink gently; low and they snap down.

try: Patch a NOISE or a sawtooth source into SPECTRUM's in. Then put a filter between them and turn its cutoff: watch the bars on the right vanish as the sound darkens.
